sources.citation: Mattei-Muller, Marie-Claude. 2003. Pémono: eslabón perdido entre mapoyo y yawarana, lenguas caribes ergativas de la Guayana noroccidental de Venezuela. Amerindia 28: 33-54.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Sec. 2.1 (comparative phonology of Mapoyo, Pémono, Yawarana). p.43: 'Un análisis fonológico más detenido es necesario para determinar la fonemicidad de las vocales largas y el rol del acento tónico en sus respectivos sistemas' -- role of stress explicitly left undetermined. Uses 'sílaba acentuada/atónica' as a conditioning context for h/glottal allophony (p.38, Yawarana ['tihpe] Var. [tih'pano] 'corto') and marks accent sporadically and variably on cited Yawarana forms (paráhwa, tahúremï ~ táhuremi, mutukú, pitšá). No statement of stress position.

Paper/poster, 175th ASA meeting (Minneapolis); abstract JASA 143:1966, doi:10.1121/1.5036469 -- the poster/slides or any follow-up write-up (UO Yawarana documentation project, NSF-DEL).

sources.note: Only instrumental study of Yawarana prominence; the abstract reports design but no results. The poster or an unpublished report would say whether any consistent stress position emerged. Ask the authors (Gildea / Cáceres Arandia / Baese-Berk, U Oregon).

sources.citation: Méndez-Arocha, Alberto. 1959. Un vocabulario yabarana con apuntes fonémicos. Antropológica 7: 63-84. Caracas: Sociedad de Ciencias Naturales La Salle.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only dedicated phonemic notes on Yabarana; Mattei-Muller 2003 shows it refers to stressed syllables, so it very likely marks stress throughout the vocabulary and may state where it falls. Publisher's site lapsed; not in the Internet Archive (only pp.47-62 of no.7 archived); HathiTrust likely search-only.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1928. Vom Roroima zum Orinoco, Bd. 4: Sprachen. Stuttgart: Strecker & Schröder (Yauarána wordlist, with his general remarks on accent notation).
